sections.text: The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them. They only obstruct the path.

It is better to do thine own duty, however lacking in merit, than to do that of another, even though efficiently. It is better to die doing ones own duty, for to do the duty of another is fraught with danger.
Arjuna asked: My Lord! Tell me, what is it that drives a man to sin, even against his will and as if by compulsion?

We had been discussing chapter three, Karma Yoga, Yoga of actions. In other words, we are trying to understand how can I transform my actions which are binding me right now into liberating entities right now, every action I do, I am bound by results which are either good or bad. And this cycle continues.
How can I transform this cycle of acting and reacting into liberating me? The goal is that the more I act, the more liberated I become. But right now, the more I act, the more bound I am -- the more I seek happiness, the more I collect unhappiness. As we discussed last time, the Sukha is something which is defined by absence of dukkha.
As long as I have dukkha of any kind, sukha cannot be experienced. 99% of my body is very healthy except my heart. We typically argue when contractors or clients find mistakes in our drawings: But look at the rest of the project, how well we have done. But I tell them that doesnt count. An error is an error; that creates problems for us.
If a car you buy is 99% perfect except the engine is not firing properly, is that a good car or a lemon? So when I have some dukkha, Im dukkhi. The more I try to achieve happiness, I somewhere along the line acquire unhappiness. If I look at my life, it is basically more unhappiness with a little happiness scattered here and there.
The happiness is experienced when I dont have to gain anything. The day I feel that I have everything I want and I dont have to acquire anything that day, I feel happy. The next moment I realize, Oh, but I forgot -- I have to also achieve this, and the unhappiness starts all over again, or the pursuit of happiness starts all over again.
So Bhagavan said there is a technique to get out of this rut of trying to get happiness and getting unhappiness in the bargain. The first thing he said is: do it for the greater good. Dont think about yourself.
Think about whether its going to help others. And then act with the first technique. Secondly, he says, all your likes and dislikes are in your senses only.
The likes and dislikes of the object reside in your senses only. If I close my eyes, there is neither a good sight nor a bad sight. Thats why when we are afraid, we close our eyes.
We dont want to see. We want to shut down that sense. So say, know that they are at your sense level.
You do not let that become yours. So you get detached from these likes and dislikes. Bhagawan also said that what can you do? You will always act according to your Prakriti Nigraha Kim karishadi.
Even a wise man, he knows what is right, what is wrong. But he cannot always act accordingly. Most doctors -- at least when I was in India and my friends were doctors, medical students, and recently graduated doctors -- they were all smoking heavily.
Even a wise man who knows all that. But because the force of those vasanas will make you only behave in that manner. Till you exhaust those vasanas or till you transcend those vasanas.
When we were children, we were hung up on little things. But as we grow up, those little attachments to toys drop away, because you transcended them. So as long as Im under the sway of vasanas, I will act according to those vasanas.
But once I dont let those vasanas overpower me -- You are going to act according to your vasanas. But you can sublimate those as I gave you examples. Dheerananda said, if you like to sing all those movie songs, convert them into Bhajans and then come and sing at the Chinmay Mission.
So you can take your vasanas and give them a direction which is more conducive to your liberation that the technique is. Mayi Karmani Sarvani Sannyasya -- you offer all your actions to me. So all your vasanas, you offer it to him.
Just like on a Shivratri. Devi said, when you offer a flower with each name, you say one of my vasanas Bhagwan, I give it to you. Thats why in our culture, all this art, music, dances, is all Krishna in it.
All those bandises which are done in all the different ragas, all about Krishna. Because they realized that to make this art a divine art, you associate Bhagavan with it. Same art, same bandishes.
You are singing, and now Krishna is in it. So all these great Ustads, who are all Muslims, they all sang Krishnas glory. All our dances all about Krishna.
Because these are our vasana. These are our natural tendency to express ourselves into art, music, dances. But rather than making them more perverted into some very lusty field, they say, sublimate those same vasanas into higher fields.
So Bhagawan said, dont let this Vasana overpower you. You find a way to exhaust your vasanas in a manner that gives you more and more joy towards the higher goal. Offer all your actions to me.
If I go to work, I say, well, Im going it for Krishna. When you have that attitude, then you will overcome all your vasanas. Then he says, adhatma cheta sa.
And you try to find out who you are. You try to figure out who you are and then continue to act in the manner which is according to your vasanas. Because Sreyan Swadharmo were gonna have Paradharmaat Swanushtita.
Sreyan Swadharma Viguna. Whatever we are doing, we always think that had I been a doctor, I would have been making more money. I didnt realize when I was going to architecture school that architects dont make much money.
Actually, our teachers told us in the very first class, very first class. Any architecture school you go. The first thing they said, if you are here to make money, there is a technology engineering college next door and medical school two blocks away.
Architecture is not for making money. But we still thought that that may be the only thing I can do. I want to be an architect.
Swadharma, thats what you liked. So Sreyan Swadharmo Vigunaha My dharma, no matter how it seems, devoid of qualities from the societys perspective, I enjoy it. But people says, youll be a starving artist.
Why do you want to be an artist? Youll be starving artist. I want to be an artist. But society says thats not really worth much.
So Sreyan Swadharma Viguna Dharma as we have defined many, many times before in this class. The law of being, what makes me who I am is my dharma. Sugar is sugar because it has its own dharma of being sweet.
If it looks like sugar, it feels like sugar. But it does not taste like sugar. When I was in science college and I studied all my education till inter science in Gujarati.
So in chemistry they will say Padarthana guna dharma nu varnankaram. Describe the characteristics of the substance. And that used to be a standard test in a chemistry.
They give you a substance. First you have to do it in an observation, smell and then tell what it is. And then the next level is.
Then you prove it by doing some experiment on it. I remember I was in interscience and there was some substance came to me. It has some very peculiar quality and I dont even remember what it was which is very rare.
And I kind of latched onto that and I saw that I went to the examiner and said this is what it is. Thats because I latched on to one particular quality which was unique to that substance. Without that, that substance cannot be that.
Dharma is that what makes that substance what it is. My swadharma is my own vasana. The texture of my mind, my personality.
It is what makes me who I am. Now that may be viguna ha. It may not be much value to others.
Anytime I read all these magazines and say what Bill Gates is doing to help the humanity, what Elon Musk is doing, what the Google guy Larry Page is doing. Im not doing anything like that. Im barely making any difference to my own familys life or my staffs life.
But thats my swadharma. This is my swadharma. Many, many years ago when I was still very, very novice in this Bhagavad Gita classes and lectures.
One thing I realized, Im at complete ease when I am in this environment. When Im talking about Bhagavad Gita or learning Bhagavad Gita in the class everywhere else Im slightly uncomfortable. So thats my swadharma.
So Bhagavan says Sreyan swadharmo Viganaha. It may not be of much value to others but your good is to act according to your dharma, your swadharma. What is your vasanas? What is your texture of your personality? Paradharmat swanusthitaat.
Then others dharma which seems much nobler or well discharged is the translation. Well discharged means he is doing it so easily. I met few years ago in a convention for this hotel owners association where I go there because I design hotels.
When I was growing up in Surat, on the street there was a Kariwala family. They basically had a grocery shop there. Their youngest child was like 4 or 5 years old when I was in college.
So he recognized me and said, arent you such and such? He said, you remember me? I was such and such from your street. Oh, you were a little kid. I dont remember you.
And I said, what do you do? He said, well, Im a hotel owner. So I said, well, remember Im an architect. He said, Rajan, I dont really develop any hotels.
I just buy hotels and sell. And he made millions doing that. He was a multimillionaire. He said, Its very easy, Rajan.
I just dont do anything. I just buy and then sell it. For him it is so easy; for me, thats a huge undertaking. You have to have what to buy and where to sell. So Paradharma Svanosthita is so well discharged by him his duties.
But for me, thats not as easy. Swadharme Nidhanam Shreyaha -- by performing your duty, you may end up dying. In other words, you continue performing your duties, in the sense of what you like, and you die doing that.
And may not accomplish anything from others perspective. But because it was your duty, it is better for you. Because that gave you the platform for exhausting your vasanas.
That gave you the platform for performing actions which give you joy. It may be more productive to go and do something else, but thats not your dharma. When I came to this country, I worked for a contractor for a while Because I did not have a job in architecture.
And he saw some potential. He said, Rajan, this is great. We need to be in business together. And after about three or four months, I left the job.
I said, oh, I got a job at architecture office. It was not even a permanent job. And he was paying me literally minimum wages.
He said, why are you doing this? You have great opportunity. But thats what I like. I want to be an architect.
I dont want to be a contractor. So that gives me joy even at the minimum wage. I felt like Im doing my job.
Paradharmo Bhayavah -- anothers dharma, when you try to emulate it, is dangerous. We architects deal with developers all the time. So after a while, we think, I can also be a developer. All these people come to me to ask advice.

These verses address one of lifes most frustrating experiences: knowing what is right but being unable to do it. Arjunas question in verse 36 resonates across millennia: What is it that drives a person to sin, even against their will, as if compelled by force? We all know this experience - the diet we break, the angry word we speak, the commitment we abandon. It feels as though some force within us overpowers our best intentions.
Before answering, Krishna identifies the real obstacles: raga and dvesha - attraction and aversion, likes and dislikes. These are not external enemies but internal tendencies embedded in our relationship with sense objects. They are paripanthinau - obstructers on the path. And then the powerful teaching on swadharma: Shreyaan swadharmo vigunah - better is ones own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed. Even death in ones own dharma is better, for anothers dharma is fraught with fear.
Today, map your raga-dveshas in one area of life. What do you find yourself irresistibly attracted to? What do you instinctively avoid or resist? These are your specific obstacles. Do not fight them directly - that only strengthens them. Instead, acknowledge them: This is raga operating. This is dvesha arising. Then return to your swadharma - your own natural path of action. Ask yourself: What is truly MY work, my calling, my nature? Am I pursuing it, or am I chasing someone elses dharma because it looks more glamorous or profitable? Remember: Paradharmo bhayavahah - anothers path is dangerous. Find your own, and walk it imperfectly but authentically.
